thread:
Ana: Customer (acct 4321) reporting ~1.5k search hits for objects whose TTL expired 3 days ago. They called DELETE API earlier and got 202 + job id 98765. Storage metadata shows tombstone, but search still returns them. KMS rotation happened last week. Need quick repro steps and whether deletion actually ran on storage side.

Sanjay: Can you paste a couple sample object IDs and the delete request id/job id? Also any API request ids from the client?

Ana: Sample IDs: obj_9a1b, obj_9a1c, obj_9a2d. Customer provided job id 98765. No client-side errors; client got 202 and a job token.

Maya: First questions: 1) did the purge worker run for that job id? 2) does storage show tombstone vs fully deleted? 3) indexer might not have reprocessed tombstones if it can't decrypt metadata after key rotation.

Ana: Storage metadata shows tombstone flag set for those objects but deletion timestamp absent. Indexer dashboard shows last processed at 2026-03-15T02:12Z, backlog 0.

indexer-bot: note: last indexer sweep started 2026-03-16T21:04Z, no rehydrate events recorded for account 4321.

Sanjay: Could be a KMS/HSM failure at purge time. Check storage logs for KMS errors around 2026-03-16T21:00-21:10.

Ana: I grepped storage logs: `2026-03-16T21:05:12Z ERROR KMSError(403) key-rotation: access denied key=key-abc obj=obj_9a1b`

Liz: That looks like a key policy mismatch applied during rotation that blocked `indexer-service` from decrypting. @Legal-Ryan do we have any holds or policy overrides for this customer?

Legal-Ryan: No litigation hold on acct 4321. I see a key policy change deployed 2026-03-16T20:58Z that removed `indexer-service` from KeyUsage for `key-abc`. Opening SRE ticket now.

Maya: SRE repro steps for root cause verification: 1) try manual decrypt via admin tool: `./kms-decrypt --key key-abc --ciphertext <blob>` 2) check HSM audit: `hsm-auditctl query --key key-abc --since 2026-03-16T20:50Z` 3) hit internal indexer rehydrate endpoint: `POST /internal/indexer/rehydrate` with `ids=[obj_9a1b]` and watch for a successful tombstone reprocess.

Sanjay: Also collect audit logs around key usage: `cloud-audit lookup --resource key-abc --start 2026-03-16T20:50 --end 2026-03-16T21:10` and storage server logs: `grep "KMSError" /var/log/storage/2026-03-16.log | grep obj_9a1b`

retention-bot: alert: TTL discrepancy detected for account=4321 policy=default-90d object_ttl=0 object_count=3

Ana: Customer asking for ETA to fully remove and stop showing in search once we fix this. What should I tell them?

Maya: If this is only a key policy block and we revert the policy so indexer can decrypt, typical flow: rehydrate/reprocess tombstones -> indexer updates search index -> search results clear within replication window (~30-60 minutes). If we need key rewrap or manual recover, could be hours.

Sanjay: I'll revert the policy and run the manual decrypt test. Owning this, ETA 45m. Will flag if HSM audit shows denied calls.

Ana: Thanks — I'll notify customer that we're investigating and expect an update in ~45m.

Sanjay: update: policy reverted at 2320001000, manual decrypt succeeded, indexer rehydrate triggered for ids [obj_9a1b,obj_9a1c,obj_9a2d]. Monitoring search delta.

Ana: Customer confirmed obj_9a1b dropped out of search results. Will monitor for full replication and close after 24h no recurrence.

Maya: Postmortem note: root cause = key policy deployment during KMS rotation that unintentionally removed indexer decrypt permission. Action: add rotation preflight to verify `indexer-service` decrypts before policy cutover and add alert for KMSError(403) spikes tied to indexer timeframe.

Legal-Ryan: Adding audit record: INC-2026-4321, no legal hold, key policy change caused visibility lag.

Ana: Closing thread once we hit 24h green for the customer. :thumbsup:
